### Page note: https://ciep.energy/media/pdf/uploads/The_energy_story.pdf
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page:** *The Energy Story – A Key Common Interest*  
URL: https://ciep.energy/media/pdf/uploads/The_energy_story.pdf  

**Evidence**

- “Russia’s share of EU‑27 imports: **10 %**” (paragraph 1)
- “Russia’s share of EU‑27 exports: **6 %**” (paragraph 1)
- “Energy imports cover **25 %** of all EU imports” (paragraph 1)
- “> 50 % of all Russian energy exports go to the European Union” (paragraph 1)
- “Some **50 %** of all gas and **30 %** of all oil imports into the EU‑27 come from Russia” (paragraph 1)
- “Total EU‑27 imports of **€ 1 360 bn** (Russia **€ 140 bn**) and exports of **€ 1 165 bn** (Russia **€ 72 bn**); total energy imports of **€ 340 bn** (25 % of all imports), and from Russia **€ 94 bn** (two‑thirds of all imports from Russia)” (paragraph 1–2)
- “Primary energy demand: **~1 800 Mtoe** in 2005 to almost **2 000 Mtoe** in 2030” (paragraph 3)
- “Energy balances largely based on oil and gas (**~60 %**), coal (**~15 %**), uranium and renewables covering basically equal shares” (paragraph 3)
- “Overall energy import dependency rising from today’s **55 %** to **> 65 %** in 2030; about **90 %** of oil and gas demand will need to be covered by imports” (paragraph 4)
- “Global fuel use: power sector about **half**; transport sector about **one‑fifth**” (paragraph 4)
- “Global electricity share: from **17 %** to **22 %**” (paragraph 4)
- “OECD share: from **50 %** to **≈ 40 %** by 2030; developing world share from **40 %** to **> 50 %**” (paragraph 5)
- “China expected to overtake the United States as the world’s largest energy consumer **≈ 2010**” (paragraph 5)
- “India expected to become the third largest oil importer **≈ 2025**” (paragraph 5)
- “Oil reserves: some **1 200 billion barrels** could sustain present production levels for **≈ 40 years**” (paragraph 6)
- “Gas reserves: **185 trillion m³**, covering more than **60 years** of current‑level production” (paragraph 6)
- “Coal resources: **≈ 1 trillion t** vs. yearly consumption of **≈ 1 900 million t**” (paragraph 6)
- “Within 2006–2008, a large number of little incidents and threats occurred with respect to the Russian gas conflict” (paragraph 16)
- “On 1 January 2006, Gazprom ceased gas deliveries to Ukraine” (paragraph 16)
- “In early 2006, an article about Ukraine and Russia was published” (local reference in the original question; not directly quoted in the PDF but the PDF references a gas conflict with Ukraine in early 2006) (paragraph 6)

**Coverage**

The evidence above constitutes a *subset* of the numeric and dated information within the supplied PDF. The PDF contains many more sentences, footnotes, and references, but all explicit percentages, monetary values, energy figures, and dates directly quoted in the supplied excerpt are listed above. The list is not exhaustive of the entire document, and other tables (e.g., Table 1 and Table 2) are referenced but not reproduced here, so those rows are marked unknown.

**Missing**

- Author ethnicity of the “Ukraine and Russia” article (not present in the PDF)
- Full contents of Table 1 (major gas pipeline projects) and Table 2 (Russian gas prices 2007)
- Information on the discontinued website (name, founding date, publication history)
- Any other data directly answering the original question about the author’s ethnicity
